next_action.description: Start step 5: settings-popup surgery in js/components/Organisms/MpiPromptBox/MpiPromptBox.js. Delete the model dropdown block (~1128-1150, guarded by `if (model) { if (modelList.length >= 1) {`) and the op dropdown (_refreshOpDropdown plus its `#settings-op-dropdown-slot`), leaving the popup as parameters only behind a cogwheel trigger. NOTE the strip refresh currently piggybacks on _refreshOpDropdown - `_refreshOpStrip()` is called from its first lines, and ten call sites call _refreshOpDropdown. When the dropdown half goes, rename the survivor to something honest (_refreshOpChoices) and keep every one of those call sites pointing at it, or the strip stops updating on media/model change. _opChoices() is already the shared list builder and stays. The existing bottom-right composite button (KREA 2 NSFW - IMAGE TO IMAGE) becomes the model button; its op half drops since the strip now shows it.

key_decisions: The op strip FLOATS above the bar (position:absolute, bottom:100%, right:var(--s-6), z-index:2) on the same layer as the media chips - it is NOT a grid row inside the bar. The user rejected the in-bar version explicitly: the bar has to keep its compact height or it covers the gallery grid and, worse, the history canvas. The strip carries its own --surface-bar background because it now sits over artwork.

A block reason APPENDS to the operation's description, never replaces it: `Image to Image - reshape an input image toward your prompt · needs 1 image`. The user's words: "needs an image" alone is almost useless, the information about the operation is much more useful.

Available (enabled, unselected) ops are --ink-1 near-white, scoped to the strip so other radio groups keep their muted --ink-3 look. The primitive's hover drops to --ink-2, which DARKENS a near-white chip, so that is overridden in MpiPromptBox.css too.

MpiRadioGroup option-level disabled now renders `aria-disabled="true"` instead of the `disabled` attribute. Chrome dispatches NO mouse events on a disabled form control, so the repo-wide [data-info] status-bar hover (statusBar.js:262) died on exactly the options that most need to explain themselves. The click handler refuses aria-disabled; CSS dims both spellings. Swept: no component passes option-level `disabled` today, and the two places reading btn.disabled (MpiOptionSelector.js:233, PromptBoxControls.js:408) use the DOM property imperatively and still work.

The strip routes clicks through Events.emit('workspace:set-operation') - the same path the radial uses - so the owning Block still validates against its live context and calls back into setOperation. Selecting directly would give the box a second, unvalidated source of truth. MpiPromptBox deliberately does NOT subscribe to that event itself.
The canonical sort lives INSIDE getAvailableCommands, not just in the strip, so every surface shares one order. The risk that this moved _pickFallbackOp's landing op is pinned by test, not assumed.

canMask rides the PromptBox's existing `workspaceKey` prop ('gallery'|'history') rather than new Block plumbing - both mount sites already set it correctly, so a gallery box cannot drift into claiming a canvas. _buildGalleryItems passes canMask:false directly because that ring IS the gallery.
`short` is the canonical-order key, not the op key: edit/krea2Edit/qwenEdit all share short 'edit' and therefore share a strip position across models.

Absent vs disabled is the load-bearing distinction. ABSENT = the model or the workspace cannot run it -> not rendered. DISABLED = the model can, the staged chips do not fit -> dim with the reason on hover.
The media strip now carries `linear-gradient(to top, var(--surface-bar), transparent)` - from the original mockup, never implemented until now.
constraints: USER PREFERENCE: never use the AskUserQuestion picker tool. Its overlay covers the screen so the user cannot read the analysis above it. Ask questions as plain text at the end of the response. ExitPlanMode is still fine.

The user's own app instance owns port 3000. Do NOT spawn a second instance - agent-launched instances become zombies serving a stale require-cache. Frontend-only changes are picked up by a plain reload, which is how steps 3-4 were verified.
npm run test:desktop cannot run while the user's app holds port 3000.

Registry-only node tests DO work and are the cheap proof: `node --test tests/op-strip-availability.test.cjs`. commandRegistry.js has zero imports, so a .cjs test can `await import` it directly (see tests/media-slot-ordinal-roles.test.cjs for the pattern).
Lint baseline: 0 errors, 1 pre-existing warning in MpiPromptBox.js (raw querySelector, now ~line 1699 after the edits). Do not chase it.
NEVER use `git stash push -- <path>` to probe history - it silently reverted a previous session's working changes. Use `git show HEAD:<path>`.
board.json and js/data/modelConstants/*.js are CO-OWNED by another session. Commit code by explicit pathspec (git commit --only <paths>), never git add -A.
MPI-337 is in place: there is NO force-DOWN. Removing media never switches the op - it goes selected+disabled, which is one of the strip's four states and must stay representable.
